Hero frame generation pass 5
Start every NBP prompt with a strong verb: "Generate", "Create", "Render". Official Google guidance — improves prompt adherence. Weak: "Mourad standing...". Strong: "Generate Mourad standing..."

Prefer positive framing over negatives in NBP prompts. "empty residential street" > "no cars". EXCEPTION: brand-binary explicit exclusions still appropriate ("No side door on cargo box") — too critical to leave to inference.

Trait locking: reuse exact same descriptor words verbatim in every prompt to prevent identity drift. "warm olive skin, short black beard, dark brown eyes, strong jawline" must not vary — never swap to "tan skin" or "black stubble".
Character unique tag: prepend a short tag (e.g. "Mourad-SV") + one-line descriptor at the start of every character prompt. Model anchors on named identities. Include tag before scene description.

Named fonts work in NBP: "Century Gothic 12px", "Impact-style", "bold clean sans-serif". Use for CTA card designs. Text-first hack: converse to generate text concepts, then request image. Do NOT use for truck-surface text — post-overlay only.

Official Google workflow: generate shot start+end keyframes with NBP Edit, pass start frame as image_url to Veo I2V. Veo animates between. Brand accuracy from hero-frame QA gate carries through. Best for predictable action pairs.

Use TNTwise rife-ncnn-vulkan fork (github.com/TNTwise/rife-ncnn-vulkan). Latest model is rife-v4.25 vs v4.6 in nihui original. TTA mode (-x flag) deprecated in v4.25 — omit it.

FFmpeg libvmaf filter scores export quality vs reference. Command: ffmpeg -i ref.mp4 -i encoded.mp4 -lavfi libvmaf=log_fmt=json:log_path=score.json:n_subsample=5 -f null -. n_subsample=5 = 4x faster. Threshold: >=90 for delivery.
NVIDIA NVENC: -c:v h264_nvenc -preset p7 -tune hq -cq 20. 3-5x faster than libx264 slow. Use for review copies; use libx264 for archive master.
VAAPI (Intel/AMD Linux): -vaapi_device /dev/dri/renderD128 -vf format=nv12,hwupload -c:v h264_vaapi -qp 19. Check device: ls /dev/dri/renderD*
WhatsApp video message = 16MB limit with lossy recompression. Document share (paperclip > Document) = 2GB no-recompression. Always deliver master as document share to owner.
For 16MB video message: bitrate_kbps = (target_MB x 8 x 1024 / duration_sec) - audio_kbps. For 30s to 15MB: (15x8x1024/30)-128 = 3900k video. Use 2-pass encoding.
H.265/HEVC: TikTok accepts HEVC but re-compresses it anyway. Instagram does NOT reliably accept H.265. Use H.264 universally for all platforms.

Cost optimization pass 2

Use 3s Kling Standard for draft iterations: $0.65 vs $1.09 at 5s. Saves $0.44/draft. 3s sufficient to evaluate motion type, identity drift, ghost-driving. Only use 5s for Pro finals. Duration param accepts int 3-15 with linear scaling.
Wan 2.6 I2V on AIMLAPI: ~$0.13/sec ($0.65/5s), medium confidence. Minimum 5s clip only — no 3s option. More expensive than Veo 3.1 Lite ($0.52/5s) but provides I2V capability. Useful Veo fallback.
Kling 2.6 Pro I2V at ~$0.091/sec ($0.46/5s) — 58% cheaper than Kling v3 Standard. CANARY REQUIRED. Not validated for character face identity. Potential use: truck-only draft shots.
NB2 (google/nano-banana-2) Google official rate: $0.067/image at 1K, $0.151 at 4K. AIMLAPI may differ. Canary required before production. Saves ~$0.125/iteration vs NBP Edit ($0.195).
AIMLAPI polling status checks are FREE. Tokens consumed only at generation submission. Poll aggressively (every 5-10s) without cost concern. Confirmed from AIMLAPI docs.
AIMLAPI has no batch discount program for video models. All savings must come from model selection and clip duration management. Enterprise plan exists but terms are negotiated individually.
Third-party blog (2026-04-26) cited Veo 3.1 Lite at $0.05/sec ($0.26/5s) vs our production-verified $0.104/sec ($0.52/5s). Keep production number for budgeting until re-verified on AIMLAPI directly.

Character consistency pass 2
Kling Element tokenization binds entire image region. Environmental content in ref image leaks into generated shots. MUST use pure flat white or green screen background for ALL Kling element refs.
Multi-shot: extract last frame of clip N (ffmpeg -sseof -0.1), use as image_url for clip N+1 alongside elements for identity lock. Separate from tail_image_url stationarity technique.
Do NOT use generated frames as refs. Each round-trip through 3D latent compounds geometry errors. By shot 3-4, identity collapses. Always re-anchor from original approved studio refs.
